chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abil Balad, from whoever narrated it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Whoever recites a verse of poetry on Friday, that is his portion/reward from that day. And the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: When you see an elder narrating traditions of the Age of Ignorance on Friday, throw a pebble at his head [even if it be] with a small stone.

key_terms.أَحَادِيثُ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: Traditions of the Age of Ignorance

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting poetry on Friday and how to handle elders narring pre-Islamic stories?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this dual instruction in *Al-Khisal*, contrasting the permissibility of poetic recitation as a means of earning reward with the specific etiquette for correcting elders who narrate pre-Islamic (*Jahiliyyah*) stories on Fridays. The directive to 'throw a pebble at his head' is interpreted by Shia scholars not as aggression, but as a gentle, non-disruptive form of rebuke or attention-grabbing to encourage the elder to transition to religious discourse.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-94 Ahmad ibn Zyad ibn Ja’far al-Hamedany - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abil Balad, who quoted that someone quoted on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

Whoever recites a poem on Friday will receive the same as reward for that day. God’s Prophet (MGB) said, ‘If you see a Sheikh narrate a tradition of the Age of Ignorance on Friday you should hit him on the head even if it be with just a small pebble.’”
